# T-1: Prioritize authoritative stale recovery

<!-- Auto-generated by `senti spec render` from spec.json.tasks[]. Do not edit manually. -->

## Goal
Separate structural artifact authority from outcome success in the integration precheck, then route a verified stale fingerprint mismatch through the existing gate-owned recovery while preserving all fail-closed boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- R1 and R2 classify structurally authoritative failed evidence before the outcome verdict.
- R3 and R4 complete one owned recovery operation and expose auditable result data.
- R5 and R6 preserve malformed and unchanged-fingerprint failures without mutation.
- R7 preserves trusted semantic evaluation and explicit rewind command guards.
- R8 supplies spec-local and affected shared regression coverage.

## Implementation Notes
Keep run-gate as the orchestration entrypoint and hide staged structural/outcome validation inside a cohesive test-artifact trust abstraction. Reuse StaleTestEvidenceMismatch and StaleIntegrationTestEvidence rather than adding a second mutation path. If recovery mutation needs stronger failure handling to satisfy R4, extend the existing recovery owner and its class invariants instead of adding caller-side cleanup. Do not weaken run-rewind-test-evidence authority checks.

## Test Strategy
Add a spec-local Node test file with a `// spec: R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7 R8` header. Reuse production-shaped fixtures to cover failed summary plus stale fingerprint recovery, failed review plus stale fingerprint recovery, unchanged failed evidence, malformed and inconsistent fingerprint matrices, invalid ownership and placeholder boundaries, recovered result fields and lifecycle/artifact effects, trusted current evidence, and explicit rewind guard rejection. Update focused shared flow tests only where the production contract changes. Run targeted tests during test-execute and full `npm test` once at final-regression.
